answer: An agent economy can make each new identity post a bond that stays locked for twenty epochs and is slashed if its answers are judged copies. The bond for the k-th join in an epoch is a base fee times k squared, so a lone honest newcomer pays almost nothing, while a farm adding n fakes at once pays a total that grows roughly with n cubed, and spreading them out ties capital up for months. A sudden plume of sign-ups shows on chain as an umber band of prices at the registration inlet that anyone can audit.
